rationale: The 85,325.2 reduce trigger set at midnight and held through morning fired with a confirmed settled 1H close of 84,047.2 (16:00-17:00 UTC / 11:00-12:00 COT), which also broke the 85,111.1 invalidatesAt and the 85,050 stop-order price flagged at morning. Price printed a fresh session low of 83,500.2 before a partial bounce to 84,308.7. Trimming about 8% of the spot book -- roughly the size of the midnight tactical add (15 USDT at 86,393.2) -- rather than the full multi-week core: daily structure (price above every daily EMA, RSI 63.94, MACD histogram still positive though decelerating) stays intact and OI fell 5.3% this session (real deleveraging, not fresh leverage building under the flush like the prior two cascades), so this reads as a sharp liquidation-amplified flush inside a still-standing daily uptrend. But the pre-set invalidation was tagged with a settled close, not just wicked, so acting on it now rather than letting a second report slide past a fired level.

message.text: Reduced the tactical tranche after the 85,325.2/85,111.1/85,050 levels all broke on a confirmed settled 1H close (84,047.2). Price bounced off a session low of 83,500.2 back to 84,308.7. New forward levels: reduceIf 83,500.2 (a settled close below the low), addIf 85,111.1 (reclaim of the former invalidation level). Watch whether the bounce holds or the low gets retested.

lesson.pattern: A reduce level held 'close but not fired' for a full report cycle before firing decisively.
lesson.insight: When a reduce level is flagged as 'closest it's been tested all week' but not yet fired, the next report can see price travel through that level AND the invalidation level AND the stop-order price in the same session if no one acts in between -- proximity warnings should raise the bar for acting on the next confirmed touch, not just the next report.
